analysis.title: Equity Strategy (Global Markets Strategy), Mislav Matejka, 02 November 2026
key_insights: Near-term wildcard is a geopolitical re-escalation after the US mid-terms, which could bring a bout of market weakness and a fresh oil spike. JPM expects any restart of the Iran conflict not to be prolonged and to end up as another dip to buy, like all geopolitics-driven dips since March. Sentiment is already very fragile.

Equities have been resilient: MSCI World is up 12% ytd (total return, USD), with SPX 3% off all-time highs and SXXP 2% off. Beneath the surface, last month's sharp rotation into Defensives erased all the gains beta sectors made in the prior 3 months. Beta is flat on the year and the Low Vol group is still losing money ytd.

JPM maintains its call, made in early October, that bond yields have peaked. It argues that the interpretation of a turn in yields will become more positive. If activity and earnings do not step lower, peaking yields let the upcycle last longer. Historically the start of Fed tightening confirmed a strong economy, and end-cycle never happened from the point of peak margins.

Q3 results reaction is mixed, but EPS growth is strong, which has produced a meaningful equity derating. Global PMIs are holding at highs and the latest IFO made a 4-year high. Inflation expectations are not rising and wage growth is soft. JPM sees big differences to the 2022 template on Tech outlook and the inflation, wages and labour backdrop.

Median Q3 EPS growth was expected at 8% y/y in both the US and Europe, but results so far are 10% (US) and 13% (Europe). Earnings breadth is improving and the lead indicator of earnings points to more upside.

P/Es have derated ytd almost everywhere. The US is at 19x forward P/E, down from 23x, and international markets look cheaper. Korea's forward P/E is down 34.6% ytd, EM down 24.6%, China down 22.4%, and the US down 12.2%.

Equity sentiment likely got overly bearish, including on France, seasonals are improving and overall equity positioning is light. JPM suggests an 'escalate in order to de-escalate' pattern is possible, so selling during derisking episodes risks being whipsawed by a favourable headline.

Fed is unlikely to get more hawkish. The Fed hiked 25bp in Sept '26 and markets expect another 55bp+ by Q4 next year. Before the conflict markets priced 60bp of cuts. JPM's forecast is a 25bp hike in Dec '26 to a 4.25% funds rate, then flat. USD has been bid for 6 months but is not cheap and is overowned.

Gold fell 20-25% after being everyone's favourite long in January. JPM sees this as an opportunity to add again, looking for the debasement trade to resume. JPM's gold forecast is $4,500 by Dec '26 vs 4,013 on 26-Oct-26.

Overweight EM vs DM (EM 14.0% allocation vs 12.2% MSCI weight; DM underweight). JPM expects EM outperformance on memory-trade stabilisation, likely reduced trade headwinds with China, and a Fed that does not get more hawkish. EM is at historical-low valuations (forward P/E 8.8 vs 11.7 at start of year) and under-owned. EM has had $75bn of equity inflows ytd vs $29.2bn in all of 2025. EM strategists favour Korea, China, Taiwan, Chile and South Africa.

Asia AI hardware basket has outperformed the Mag-7 by over 70% since the start of 2025 despite a recent sell-off. JPM sees the recent weakness in EM AI hardware names as a tactical buying opportunity, with supply-demand tightness expected for at least 2-3 more quarters. Valuations are rich. Top-20 Asia AI names are down 14% to 65% from peak (SK Hynix -56%, Samsung Electronics -41%, Kioxia -65%).

Overweight Eurozone (11.0% allocation vs 8.7% weight). Eurozone was a relative loser from the Iran conflict and is disadvantaged when Tech leads given its Value-tilted composition, but activity (IFO at 4-year high, PMIs in expansion), loan growth, German fiscal stimulus and low positioning support it. Eurozone EPS is forecast +24.0% in 2026 and +12.3% in 2027 (+12% ex-Discretionary), after a -4.5% fall in 2025. Most growth comes from improving margins.

French political risk is a headwind but largely priced. CAC40 P/E relative is at record lows, French spreads are near record wide, and 80% of CAC40 revenues come from outside France. Catalysts: the budget passing by year-end and a centrist gaining ground. Polls point to a far-left (Melenchon) vs far-right (Le Pen) run-off for the 2027 presidential election, which JPM thinks may not come to pass. JPM prefers Eurozone domestics over French domestics, and Eurozone vs French Banks, and non-domestic French names.
Within Eurozone JPM favours Core (Germany, France) over Periphery (Italy, Spain) and expects the periphery outperformance to end.

Neutral Japan (6.0% allocation vs 5.7% weight): JPM took profits after Topix rose over 60% from the April '25 lows. Valuations and positioning look fuller. Foreign flows are at a decade high. JPM thinks consensus is wrong and JPY could strengthen, citing the rate differential and recent BOJ intervention. It stays OW Japanese Banks vs market and vs global Banks (trade open since April '23). JPM forecasts the Japan 10Y at 3.05% by Dec '26 (2.78% now).

Neutral UK (3.0% allocation vs 3.5% weight): large valuation discount, highest dividend yield of the big DMs, immune to AI cannibalisation and unwind risks, and a good place to hide in risk-off, but it lacks medium-term catalysts and is a low-beta defensive market. UK Autumn Budget 2026 was a stability event: banks +1.1% on a less punitive surcharge, homebuilders -6.0%, Entain +3.6%, Evoke +3.7%.

Neutral US (73.0% allocation vs 73.3% weight): activity is robust and nominal growth is well above nominal yields, but concerns are elevated positioning, Tech direction, valuation premium (US 12m fwd P/E 19.0x, 12% above 20Y median), K-shaped consumer, and more Fed hikes being priced. JPM expects SPX to make fresh highs into year-end on the earnings uptrend and Tech stabilisation. US households hold close to record equity share of assets.

Tech is not an outright sell. Hyperscalers are the cheapest since 2012 on relative P/E and Semis trade as if the cycle has ended, which JPM sees as too negative. JPM calls for re-engaging in the AI trade, but not a return to past dominance because monetization concerns will persist. SOX fell 28% and KOSPI 39% from peak. Memory fundamentals are strong, with demand-supply balance unlikely before 2028 and pricing rising into 2027.

JPM stays cautious on AI cannibalisation areas (Software, Business Services, Media) but called in March for closing shorts there. Fundamental concerns persist, though the group is likely to keep trading better tactically. Software is not seen as a good naked short; a Semis vs Software pair trade is more interesting. Europe Software underperformed the market by more than 50% to the July lows.

Sector stance: OW Metals & Mining, Capital Goods, Construction Materials, Luxury, Semis; UW Energy, Media, Staples, Insurance, Software; Neutral Banks, Utilities, Healthcare, Autos, Telecoms, Real Estate, Chemicals, Tech Hardware. European allocation: Materials OW 8.0% vs 5.4%, Industrials OW 21.0%, Discretionary OW 8.0%, Energy UW 3.0%, Staples UW 6.0%.

Energy equities are UW: the sector has re-priced almost entirely in lockstep with Brent, leaving no valuation buffer. A concrete US-Iran deal would bring oil back toward pre-crisis levels. Hormuz crude flows have recovered to 17.5 mbd (98% of pre-war) while product exports are only 3 mbd (58%) as of mid September. Increased supply from UAE, Colombia, Iraq and Venezuela is also expected. Energy earnings estimates are up 55% since the conflict began, a tailwind JPM calls temporary; it advises locking in gains.

European Banks (Neutral): JPM sees fundamentals as supportive (healthy NIMs, credit growth, NPL decline, CET1 projected 14% under Basel 4, absorb provisions above 250bp) and advises using recent weakness to add. It prefers non-French Banks over French Banks. Insurance is UW, with premiums falling and credit spreads set to widen.

European Defense: JPM turned more positive after a year of weakness and derating (sector outperformed by more than 90% from 2024 to its Q3 '25 peak before the derating). It prefers modernization plays (drones, electronic warfare, munitions replenishment, space) over legacy platforms. Total European defence budget is forecast to grow at a 9% CAGR 2025E-2030E.

Value and small caps: JPM has been positive on Value in Europe since end '24 and looks for more upside. US small caps (S&P600) have derated to lows relative to large caps and SPW (equal-weight S&P) is rebounding vs SPX as yields peak.

Germany: structural primary deficit widens from -0.7% of GDP (2025) to -1.8% (2026) and -2.3% (2027), roughly 2% of GDP of easing over two years. The EUR 500bn infrastructure fund is real; the issue is timing. By August 2026 the cumulative federal deficit was EUR 22bn wider y/y, about half the full-year widening implied by the 2026 budget.

China: JPM economists see scope for a positive surprise on fiscal support, with consumption-focused measures. JPM forecasts 2026 consumption support of about 700bn yuan (0.5% of GDP) vs 596bn in 2025. Sentiment toward China growth is sceptical, geopolitical risks eased after the Trump-Xi meeting, and China is OW in EM. CSI 300 YTD for China is -19.4% (LC).
Credit spreads have widened somewhat since the conflict began but remain tight historically; default rates are low. Eurozone private loan growth is improving and money-supply indicators lead PMIs.

US midterm elections: recent polling shows Democrats with strong momentum. JPM lays out scenarios by theme (blue wave, gridlock, Republican status quo) for fiscal deficits, regulation and M&A, trade, affordability and AI infrastructure. Seasonals: Q4 is typically strong for equities.

Central bank balance sheets have been contracting in aggregate: G3 aggregate balance sheet projections move from $18.4tn (2024) to $13.8tn (2025e), $17.3tn (2026e) and $16.7tn (2027e). Term premia may need to rise further and US deficits are elevated.

JPM macro forecasts: US real GDP 2.3% (2025), 2.4% (2026E per one table, 2.3% in another), 2.2% (2027E); Eurozone 1.0% (2026E), 1.5% (2027E); China 4.5% (2026E); global CPI 3.7% in 4Q26. 10Y yield forecasts: US 5.05% by Dec 26 (4.92% on 30-Oct), Euro area 3.15%, UK 5.10%, Japan 3.05%. DXY forecast 102.4 by Dec 26 (102.2 now) and 104.1 by Sep 27.

Index targets: MSCI Eurozone Dec '26 target 420 vs 380 current (11% upside); FTSE 100 Dec '26 target 11,000 vs 10,722 (3% upside). Asset allocation: Equities OW 65% vs 60%, Bonds neutral 30%, Cash UW 5% vs 10%.

Thematic baskets highlighted: Eurozone Fiscal Stimulus (JPEZFIST), Ukraine-Russia rebuild (JPUKRCFR), Trade Uncertainty names (JPEUTFS), winners from lower oil (JPDEOILL), and AI cannibalisation basket (JPEUAIL). JPM also argues a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire could be a positive surprise, noting a contrarian view may be warranted.

Oil context: Brent spiked after the Iran attack, with sensitivity of equities to oil reduced. After Brent spikes of 50%+, S&P500 12m forward returns were positive most of the time (73% hit ratio positive, median +14%). US energy consumption as a share of GDP is far below historical levels.

Basic Resources/Mining held at OW since the March '25 double upgrade. Cushion vs spot metals has reopened, supported by China outlook and a potentially weaker USD.
European Energy equities UW: priced in lockstep with Brent with no valuation buffer, and earnings tailwind seen as temporary.
Nebius is 15% of the MSCI Europe Software constituent table and is up 90% ytd, listed in that table.

Electrification, AI and datacenter demand, fiscal spending and record margins; re-enter after pullback.
Strong pricing and volumes support margins; supported by activity rebound and fiscal support despite EU ETS reform fears.
Korea growth and China recovery with positive wealth effects; sector underperformed by almost 35% ytd.
AI demand and DRAM price surge, memory demand-supply balance unlikely before 2028, cleaner positioning.
Priced in lockstep with Brent, no valuation buffer, expected supply increases, temporary earnings tailwind.
Weak pricing power and demand, rising COGS inflation risk.
AI disruption of business models and pressure on margins; earnings momentum rolling over, though not a good naked short.
AI uncertainty, persistent earnings downgrades, unattractive valuations.
Falling premiums, elevated claims inflation and potential spread widening.
Supportive fundamentals and valuations but French election and spread risks; buy weakness in Europe, long Japan Banks vs global Banks.
Bond proxy that benefits if yields fall; renewables favoured within the sector.
Derated meaningfully so risk/reward improving; prefers modern capabilities (drones, EW, munitions, space) over legacy platforms.
Cheap valuations but no clear near-term tailwind; weak earnings momentum, limited patent cliff risk.

earnings_insights: Q3 median EPS growth was expected at 8% y/y in the US and Europe; results reported so far are 10% (US) and 13% (Europe), per JPM (consensus expectation vs reported actuals to date).

S&P500 2026e EPS growth consensus is +34.5% (2027e +18.1%); MSCI Europe 2026e +22.0% (2027e +9.4%); MSCI Eurozone 2026e +24.0% (2027e +12.3%); Japan FY +25.9%; EM +75.7%; MSCI World +30.3% (all consensus estimates, IBES).
Eurozone earnings were down 4.5% in 2025 (reported) and are forecast to rebound strongly (+24.0% in 2026e, about +12% ex-Discretionary); the bulk of growth is margin improvement.
Mag-7 earnings growth is estimated at 21% for Q3'26e vs 31% in Q2 as shown in the chart series, with S&P500 ex Mag-7 at 10% to 13% range; Alphabet and Meta adjusted EPS used for Q3.
Korea's 2026e EPS growth consensus is +334%, Taiwan +69%, MSCI EM +76% (IBES consensus), driven by memory and AI hardware.
Energy sector EPS estimates in Europe are up about 55% since the Iran conflict began, and Energy has been delivering better earnings than projections; JPM sees this tailwind as temporary.
Sector analysts expect a subdued reporting season for European Staples, with price deceleration, weaker US demand and possibly cautious outlooks.

risk_factors: Geopolitical re-escalation of the Iran conflict after the US mid-terms and a fresh oil price spike.
Very fragile investor sentiment, so shocks can cause outsized moves.
Fed hikes being priced (55bp+) could end up on the high side; further hawkishness would hurt P/Es.
Tech direction and AI monetization concerns; hyperscaler capex turning free cash flow negative.
French political and fiscal risk, widening French spreads and contagion.
Japan: loose fiscal policy driving JPY depreciation or a JGB yield spike.
Elevated US valuations and concentration; US household equity ownership near record.
K-shaped consumer and weakening labour market; elevated hiring uncertainty.
Energy prices spiking further, which would hit the consumer and Eurozone/EM energy importers.
USD strength and widening real rate differentials (headwind for EM and commodities).
Credit spreads widening, which would hurt Insurance and Banks.
US fiscal deficits and term premium rising.
vol_and_positioning: Overall equity positioning is rather light: US Tactical Positioning Monitor, speculative S&P500 futures positions and asset manager positioning are far from stretched; Europe positioning is almost as low as January 2025.
Sentiment is very fragile / downbeat: AAII bull-bear is depressed, though seasonals (Q4) are getting better.
USD net positioning is stretched again and the dollar is overowned; JPM trade-weighted USD is not cheap.
Semis positioning is cleaner after the recent sell-off; momentum factor unwind occurred mid-year.
Low Vol baskets are performing poorly (US and European Low Vol baskets), and JPM stays cautious on Low Vol.
US Treasuries turned oversold (RSI) at the start of October when JPM called the peak in yields.
US households hold close to record levels of equities as a share of total assets; asset manager S&P500 futures positioning is elevated vs average.
Flows: US equity funds took $63.9bn in the last month and $523bn ytd; UK funds had -$14.7bn ytd and Europe ex UK -$12.5bn ytd (EPFR as of 28 Oct 2026); Japan +$39.8bn ytd.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: risk of re-escalation after the US mid-term elections, with a possible fresh oil spike; JPM expects any restart to be short and a dip to buy.
Oil volatility around newsflow on any US-Iran ceasefire; a concrete deal would return oil toward pre-crisis levels.
Strait of Hormuz remains a chokepoint carrying about 20% of world oil supply; crude flows 98% recovered, refined products at 58%.
Trump-Xi meeting eased geopolitical risks with China; US-China effective tariffs are lower and the worst of the trade uncertainty appears behind.
France: 2027 presidential election odds point to a Le Pen vs Melenchon run-off; Le Pen most likely to win overall, and no centrist in the second round could pressure risk assets.
Russia-Ukraine ceasefire probability shown as a chart; JPM suggests a contrarian view that a ceasefire could be a positive surprise.
US mid-term elections: Democrats have strong polling momentum; scenario analysis covers blue wave, gridlock and Republican status quo.
Public support for US military intervention in the Iran war is shown at 41%, the lowest in a historical comparison.
cross_bank_references: Our fixed income team's view that bond yields move lower is cited as support for UK dividend strategies, if vindicated.
JPM's own EM Equity Strategy, Commodity Strategy, Economics and sector research teams are referenced throughout; no other banks are cited.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM expects any restart of the Iran conflict to be short and another dip to buy, like all geopolitics-driven dips since March; after 50%+ oil spikes equities were higher 12 months later most of the time (73% hit ratio).
tension_points.bear_case: Sentiment is already very fragile, and a re-escalation could bring a bout of weakness and a fresh oil spike, with Energy, Eurozone and EM most exposed as energy importers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A prolonged restart of the Iran conflict with a fresh oil price spike and inflation fears worsening would invalidate the dip-to-buy view.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields peaked in early October; peak yields allow the upcycle to be more sustained, Cyclicals and Financials benefit, and Fed is unlikely to get more hawkish.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets are pricing 55bp+ of Fed hikes, defensives rallied as investors feared the cycle outlook, and US P/Es are high against rising real yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Activity and earnings taking a clear step lower, or inflation fears worsening, would break the call.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are the cheapest since 2012 on relative P/E, Semis trade as if the cycle has ended, memory fundamentals are strong into 2027-28 and positioning is cleaner.
tension_points.bear_case: Monetization concerns persist, hyperscaler free cash flow has turned negative on capex, and AI will not return to past dominance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further decline in hyperscaler capex or earnings peaking would undermine the re-engagement call.

tension_points.bull_case: Eurozone activity, credit growth, German fiscal stimulus and low positioning support an OW, with cheap valuations relative to the US.
tension_points.bear_case: The region is more energy-import exposed, has a Value-tilted index when Tech leads, and faces French political risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Escalation or persistence of the Iran conflict or French contagion would expose more downside.
